outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a serial_only_pass outcome. The parallel solution failed because its coordinated plan depended on a parser child and a test child that were still active when the parent/swarm was cancelled. The final visible package still lacked math_verify.parser, so import-dependent scripts and official tests could not run. The serial solution avoided that lifecycle break by using one end-to-end actor to copy a complete upstream source tree including parser.py, install it, and verify it locally before closure.
parallel_contributors: The parallel parent launched five subagents and delegated the required parser implementation to a child.
The parser child was cancelled before delivery, the swarm result reported two aborted children, and a surviving child observed ModuleNotFoundError for math_verify.parser.
serial_contributors: The serial actor copied a complete source and test tree including parser.py before installing the package.
The serial actor confirmed imports, ran 283 local tests plus spec examples, and then the official evaluation passed 192 of 192.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial run used the upstream math-verify 0.8.0 source distribution as a behavioral reference; the parallel run attempted a hand-built, delegated implementation.
Several parallel children produced scoped files successfully, so the failure is not explained by every component being poor code; the missing parser artifact is the concrete implementation gap.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed: the parent assigned parser.py, grader.py, support modules, packaging, and tests to concrete children; the parser owner was cancelled rather than absent.
The parent retained the orchestration role and no complete incompatible component set awaited reconciliation; the direct failure was loss of the parser child before integration.
Packaging and final files had an assigned child and many package artifacts were written; the blocker was missing parser implementation, not absent assembly ownership.
The parent owned the end-to-end swarm handoff and planned collection; pipeline closure was cut off by cancellation, not left ownerless in the initial plan.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; several child implementations and project files were written concurrently after delegation.
The parallel run did not perform all investigation as a first phase before implementation; grader, support, packaging, and tests progressed while the parser child probed.
The indispensable parser path did not merely receive too little capacity while others consumed it; the directly observed boundary is active child cancellation before delivery.
The five-agent fan-out and timeout are screening signals, but the retained event is the more specific cancellation of required active children; no separate fan-out exhaustion episode is needed.
The parser brief was broad, but the observed adverse event is explicit cancellation before parser delivery; retaining oversized scope would duplicate the same chain.
The parent's parser delegation included detailed parser behavior and smoke-check obligations; there is no known parent-held task requirement shown absent from the child brief.
Support modules referenced parser and grader in the expected package API, but no incompatible independently produced interfaces are shown; parser.py was absent rather than mismatched.
No known finding, constraint, or checkpoint is shown being omitted during transfer and then causing repeated work or wrong action.
Completed child summaries were available, but the run ended at cancellation; there is no demonstrated large handoff that the parent failed to reduce.
No receiver is shown consuming a superseded workspace or requirement state; the final issue is a missing component, not stale transferred information.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; there was no delivered parser result to conflict with other components.
The parallel parent did not make a whole-task completion or acceptance decision; the run was cancelled and later failed official evaluation.
There is no replacement or retry of the parser or test worker after cancellation, so no repeated work without inherited checkpoint is visible.

candidates.reason: The parser child was active and responsible for the required parser implementation, but it was explicitly cancelled before delivering parser.py; the parent's swarm result then showed aborted children and the package remained unimportable.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required parser implementation never reached the workspace, leaving math_verify.parser absent and causing the official evaluation to fail 0 of 192 tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The lack of takeover is downstream of the same cancellation event; there was no separate post-failure recovery window before parent closure.

candidates.reason: No complete directly promotable parser or compatible whole-package candidate existed; the parser component was unfinished and unreturned.
No relevant integrated verification succeeded before a later merge; the package remained unimportable and integrated tests did not pass.
The required parser implementation was never completed or retrievable; completed grader and support work was not the missing implementation join.
The verifier/test child did not produce a concrete completed finding that was trapped below the parent; it was interrupted while waiting for importability.
Although cancelled children left required work unfinished, this is the same cancellation chain retained as Early Child Termination, not an independent takeover episode.
No completed child result containing the missing parser or decisive verifier finding was visible to the parent and ignored.
The parent did wait on the swarm until cancellation, but the direct and more specific evidence is active child termination, not missed inspection of available progress.
Children wrote different scoped files, but no competing implementations claiming the same behavior or interface were completed and left for reconciliation.
No raw event shows two live agents editing the same source or configuration file and forcing reconciliation.
No agent is shown replacing or wholesale rewriting non-entry source produced or actively owned by another agent.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another actor owned or used it.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs and invalidating final-tree work.
The agents wrote into one workspace, but the observed consequence was a missing cancelled parser, not an unstable-state or provenance problem from unisolated writes.
No generated file, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as a stable reference environment.
